newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain rate seen unchanged - Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain rate seen unchanged - Reuter poll.

text.p: The Bank of Spain is likely to keep its key money rate unchanged at 6.75 percent on Friday at its regular repo auction, a Reuter poll found on Thursday.

All 10 financial analysts polled said the central bank would rather wait for November inflation data to confirm a descending trend in consumer prices before sanctioning its seventh official rate cut of the year.
But after lower-than-expected October inflation data they also considered there was a real possibility of a rate cut in the short term.
"I'd say tomorrow is too early, but we have a 40 percent chance of seeing a lower key money market rate," said Alfredo Urrutia, economist at Societe Generale in Madrid.
October inflation, which rose a modest 0.1 percent monthly and 3.5 percent yearly, boosted the market's expectations of a fresh rate cut before year-end.
Earlier on Thursday, Bank of Spain governor Luis Angel Rojo said it is likely Spanish inflation will end the year at 3.3 percent, versus a previous forecast of 3.5 percent.
This boosted the market's hopes of a cut, dealers said.

Analysts said expectations are for an official rate cut of 0.25 - 0.50 percent because they expected inflation to ease gradually to three percent and then break that level by the first quarter of 1997.
But analysts added that Bank of Spain would likely wait for November prices data, due on December 13.
A Bank of Spain repo is also scheduled for that day. The subsequent repo is on December 24.
On October 3 the Bank of Spain cut its key rate 50 basis points to 6.75 percent.
The rate started the year at nine percent.
